correctness.rationale: Equal colours within a layer give a transposition fixing all term values. For b=1 a same-colour lower point and the upper point remain indistinguishable under implication because their successor sets are respectively the pair and the singleton, and both operands agree on the pair. For b>=2 a nonempty proper upper restriction is a generator X contained in B, and X joined with its negation gives B. For b=1 the meet of the generators true at the upper point gives B. The resulting two Boolean intervals have definable relative complements and separating generators, so generate all upsets. For b>=2 the c all-one upper columns are exactly the free positions for lower words. Partition-lattice inversion on upper rows forbids equality, yielding the signed-Stirling sum over j blocks, with 2^j-1 permitted column types. For b=1 the all-one lower subword is forbidden, giving 2^c-1 choices. The two capacities yield the ranks, and independent injective codes attain them. The boundary k=0 gives zero generating tuples for both cases. An independent bounded replay checked 1,653 actual closures for small sizes through (a,b)=(2,3) against the criterion and formulas; finite only. The recorded 4,052 source checks were inspected, not executed.
residual_risks: The replay is finite; unrestricted correctness rests on the term and inversion arguments, not on formal verification.
